# Results — Study 424 (Ease of Movement) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — Richard Arms'
Ease of Movement (EOM, 14-bar) on daily bars, turned into a **long/flat daily timing
rule** (long when EOM > 0, flat otherwise), entered with one execution lag (signal at the
close of *t*, position held over *t+1*), measured **NET of 1 bp/leg** and **excess of
cash**, and raced against buy-and-hold, an SMA(50/200) cross, and MACD(12/26/9). Headline
tape: **SPY**. As-of **2026-05-31** (each tape trimmed to the last complete month so no
partial month enters the statistics). SPY: **n = 5,013** daily bars (~20 years).*

## Data stamp (trimmed to as-of 2026-05-31)

| Ticker | Window | n | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| SPY  | 2006-06-26 → 2026-05-29 | 5013 | `dfbb7ba4dbe2` |
| QQQ  | 2006-06-26 → 2026-05-29 | 5013 | `4fde85657fb1` |
| IWM  | 2006-06-26 → 2026-05-29 | 5013 | `a2e85b11a8f4` |
| DIA  | 2006-06-26 → 2026-05-29 | 5013 | `27b78757ebc3` |
| EFA  | 2006-06-26 → 2026-05-29 | 5013 | `04be1a24c190` |
| EEM  | 2006-06-26 → 2026-05-29 | 5013 | `a8d1d9711bfb` |

Yahoo! daily bars, `auto_adjust=True` (total-return-adjusted closes — dividends folded in).
Excess-of-cash uses a flat 0% risk-free in the stamped run (the race is excess-vs-excess,
so a constant rf cancels in the Sharpe comparison); borrow is charged on short days only.

## The honest test — SPY, EOM(14) long/flat, NET 1 bp, excess of cash

| Arm | Sharpe (ann) | HAC *t* | ann. return | max DD | exposure | turnover |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **EOM long/flat (net)** | **+0.684** | **+3.18** | +7.68% | −29.7% | 0.641 | 23.0/yr |
| EOM long/flat (gross) | +0.704 | +3.28 | +7.91% | −29.7% | 0.641 | 23.0/yr |
| Buy & hold | +0.657 | — | **+12.78%** | **−55.2%** | 1.000 | 0 |
| SMA(50/200) cross (net) | +0.679 | +3.41 | — | — | — | — |
| MACD(12/26/9) (net) | +0.579 | +2.89 | — | — | — | — |

- **The rule's returns are genuinely distinguishable from zero.** EOM long/flat earns a
  net annual Sharpe of **+0.684** with **HAC *t* = +3.18** — clearing the desk's *t* ≥ 2
  bar. That is a *real* signal: an "effortless" advance (price rising on light volume)
  does precede positive forward returns.

## Does it beat the benchmarks? — the difference tests (positive *t* = EOM wins)

| Comparison | ann. difference | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| EOM − Buy&Hold | **−5.10%** | **−1.71** |
| EOM − SMA(50/200) | −1.67% | −0.61 |
| EOM − MACD | +1.23% | +0.74 |

- **It does not beat buy-and-hold.** The Sharpe edge (0.684 vs 0.657) is marginal and the
  *return* is far lower (+7.68% vs +12.78%); the difference test is **negative** (*t* =
  −1.71). EOM's only genuine win is a halved drawdown (−30% vs −55%) — i.e. it is
  **de-risked beta**, the same thing any trend filter buys you, not alpha.
- **It is statistically indistinguishable from a plain SMA(50/200) cross** (*t* = −0.61),
  the simplest possible trend rule, and only marginally edges MACD (*t* = +0.74, not
  significant). The volume weighting that is EOM's whole selling point adds nothing over a
  price-only moving-average cross.

## Sign-shuffle permutation placebo (gross Sharpe, 2,000 draws)

Keeping the realised holding durations but flipping each episode's sign by a fair coin:

| | Sharpe |
|---|--:|
| Observed EOM (gross) | +0.704 |
| Null mean | −0.010 |
| **p-value** | **0.0005** |

The timing dates carry directional information that a sign-shuffle cannot reproduce — the
signal is not an artefact of the holding-period structure.

## Cost sweep (SPY long/flat, net)

| round-trip cost | net Sharpe | HAC *t* | ann. return |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bp (gross) | +0.704 | +3.28 | +7.91% |
| 1.0 bp | +0.684 | +3.18 | +7.68% |
| 2.0 bp | +0.664 | +3.08 | +7.45% |
| 5.0 bp | +0.602 | +2.77 | +6.76% |
| 10.0 bp | +0.499 | +2.28 | +5.61% |

At ~23 round-trips/yr the rule survives realistic costs (still *t* > 2 at 10 bp). Costs are
not what kills it — the benchmark race is.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`) with a planted volume-coupled
persistence edge, the same engine recovers an EOM edge **only when the edge is planted**,
and reads ≈ 0 when it isn't (long/short, gross, cost 0):

| Planted edge | EOM gross Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| −0.10 (reversal) | −0.501 | −1.71 |
| 0.00 (martingale) | −0.094 | −0.31 |
| +0.30 | +0.483 | +1.28 |
| +0.60 | +2.384 | +4.92 |
| +1.00 | +9.423 | +14.25 |

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** SPY EOM(14) long/flat net Sharpe **+0.684**, HAC *t* = **+3.18**
  (clears *t* ≥ 2), sign-shuffle permutation *p* = **0.0005**, robust across smoothing
  windows 14–40 and confirmed on QQQ/DIA. An "effortless" advance does carry forward
  information — EOM is a genuine, if weak, momentum/trend detector.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** It does **not** beat buy-and-hold (vs-B&H *t* = −1.71, +7.68%
  vs +12.78%/yr) and is **statistically indistinguishable from a price-only SMA(50/200)
  cross** (vs-SMA *t* = −0.61). Its only edge is a halved drawdown — *de-risked beta*, not
  alpha. Anything you'd get from EOM you'd get cheaper from a two-line moving-average rule.
- **Better than a moving-average cross? — NOT SUPPORTED.** EOM's volume weighting — the
  one thing that distinguishes it from a plain SMA cross — buys no measurable advantage
  (Δ Sharpe −0.005, vs-SMA *t* = −0.61). The "ease of movement" story is real momentum
  wearing a volume costume.
